findings.title: The page data-as-of timestamp is never pinned to the document's at, so a regression that showed the wrong time would ship green

evidence.value: site/index.html:380 - asOf.innerHTML is the template literal 'data as of ' + esc(when(lastRefresh.at)) + the optional ' (stale)', or the empty string when info is null
PBI-008 L-4: 'The time comes from at, rendered through esc(). ... Each case is pinned by a page check.'

findings.impact: All five new checks assert only the 'data as of ' prefix, the presence or absence of the word stale, and the class name. None compares the rendered text with the time the document holds, and none feeds an at containing markup, so neither 'the time comes from at' nor 'rendered through esc()' is actually pinned. Replacing when(lastRefresh.at) with when(Date.now()) - the exact failure FR-104 and FR-105 exist to prevent, a board that always claims to be current - would leave all 94 checks green; only the separate stale marker would still betray it. The headline output of the feature is therefore unprotected against future edits.
findings.remediation: Add one assertion to the 5-minute case that the rendered text carries the time the document holds rather than any time - for example compute the expected string from the same locale formatter the page uses and assert equality, or assert that two different at values in the same render produce two different texts. Separately, feed an at made of a valid timestamp followed by an img-onerror fragment once and assert the output is escaped, which pins the esc() clause of L-4.

findings.title: A non-string at (null, 0, true) makes the header claim 'data as of 01:00, 1 Jan' instead of staying silent, so a corrupt record reads as a 1970 board

evidence.value: const asOfInfo = now => { if (!lastRefresh) return null; const at = new Date(lastRefresh.at); return isNaN(at) ? null : { stale: now - at.getTime() > STALE_MS }; };

node: new Date(null) -> 1970-01-01T00:00:00.000Z (valid); new Date(0) -> valid; new Date(true) -> 1970-01-01T00:00:00.001Z (valid); new Date of empty string, [], {}, undefined or 'not-a-time' -> Invalid Date
PBI-008 L-4: 'With no meta/lastRefresh document, or an unreadable at, the header shows no data as of text and logs no error.'

findings.impact: The malformed-at boundary is handled as a single representative value rather than as a class. new Date() coerces null, 0 and true to valid 1970 dates, so a record whose at is any of those renders 'data as of 01:00, 1 Jan (stale)' rather than the silence L-4 requires. It fails safe - no crash, no console error, and the text is marked stale - and both writers of the record (refresh.py here, the collector in PBI-019) are controlled and write a string, so the blast radius is a misleading header on an already-corrupt document, not a broken page. The page check pins only the string case 'not-a-time', so the gap is invisible to the suite.
findings.remediation: Require a string before parsing - test typeof lastRefresh.at against 'string' and return null otherwise, before calling new Date - and extend the existing unreadable-at page check to cover the class rather than one member: at least null, a number and a boolean alongside 'not-a-time'.

evidence.value: def test_nothing_to_push(self): [comment: every plan now sets meta/lastRefresh, so nothing to push no longer occurs] self.o.pushed(); code, out, _ = self.main(); assertEqual(code, 0); assertEqual(keys(json.loads(out)), {LAST})
exporters/refresh.py main(): the branch 'if p is None: print(nothing to push); return 0' is gone

findings.impact: The restated test does cover something real - that main() exits 0 and prints a one-write plan when nothing else changed - so it is not a weakened test. But its name asserts a state the code can no longer reach, and a reader grepping for 'nothing to push' now lands on a test that proves the opposite. The same applies, more mildly, to Plan.test_commit_then_nothing_to_push. The companion rename in Plan (test_nothing_to_push_removes_a_stale_pending_file became ..._replaces_a_stale_pending_file) shows the right treatment was available and was applied elsewhere in the same diff.
findings.remediation: Rename to something that names the new behaviour, for example test_a_quiet_tick_prints_only_the_last_refresh_write, and rename Plan.test_commit_then_nothing_to_push to match; keep the explanatory comment.

findings.title: The plan() docstring gained a 137-character run-on line, breaking the file's own wrapping and burying the MassDelete sentence

evidence.value: lines 108-110: '...records it as pending; the writes' / 'always include the set of meta/lastRefresh. Raises MassDelete, leaving nothing pending, for a delete that looks like a broken export,' / 'and AnswersRefused, ...'
the surrounding docstring and body lines wrap at roughly 115-120 characters; the new line 109 is 137 and starts a new sentence mid-line

findings.impact: Cosmetic only - no behaviour depends on it - but the new clause was inserted without re-wrapping, so the line runs past the file's own width and the 'Raises MassDelete' sentence now begins in the middle of a line. It makes the most load-bearing docstring in the module harder to scan, and that paragraph is exactly what the next reader consults to learn that every plan writes meta/lastRefresh.
findings.remediation: Re-wrap the three docstring lines to the file's usual width so each sentence starts at the left margin, for example putting 'Raises MassDelete, ...' on its own line.

follow_ups.ref: FR-103's two halves stamp at in different ISO forms
follow_ups.note: refresh.py writes strftime of %Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ (ending in Z), as PBI-008 L-1 prescribes; PBI-019 section 4.8 writes isoformat(timespec=seconds) (ending in +00:00). Both are timezone-aware, both satisfy the lastRefresh shape's strict datetime (Python 3.11+ fromisoformat accepts Z) and both parse with JS new Date(), so this is not a defect - but nothing downstream should ever compare the two as strings, and a future consumer that sorts or dedupes lexically would be surprised. Worth one line in the PBI-019 spec or in the record shape's comment.
